name: equal_effort
description: PLACEHOLDER -- NOT RUNNABLE AS SHIPPED. Isolates evaluation quality from search volume by giving DeepSetsBotExp whatever extra wall clock it needs to evaluate the SAME number of positions per turn as the stock-speed baseline, instead of the same wall clock. The answer to 'is the network better, or is the heuristic agent just searching more?' is this matchup's win rate. Fill in the two TBDs from a calibration run before submitting anything.
_why_alpha0_is_zero: SOT_ALPHA0=0 on both the matchup and the calibration block, and it is load-bearing. The question here is about the NETWORK as an evaluator, so the agent measured must be the network-only one, and the calibration must be run on the same agent that is benchmarked -- calibrating at 0.7 and running at 0.0 would match the wrong agent's throughput. At alpha0=0 the pure-network short circuit in Evaluate() fires on every leaf and one counted evaluation is exactly one ONNX forward pass. NOTE this is a definitional argument, not a throughput one: the blend also runs the heuristic inside the same counted evaluation, but that costs only ~1.6% of throughput (paired over 6 seeds), not the factor of 1.8 an earlier version of this note claimed. See experiments/README.md, 'Counting evaluations'.
_calibration_so_far: Local pilot, 2026-09-22, 10 games, SOT_ALPHA0=0, both sides at scale 1.0, --timeout 12.
NOT a substitute for a cluster run -- different hardware, and n=10 is not enough.
DeepSetsBotExp   9459 evals/turn pooled  (106,891 /game, sd 3825 across games)
SakkirinaScaled 76699 evals/turn pooled  (905,048 /game, sd 31776 across games)
ratio r = 8.11x per turn pooled, 8.47x per game pooled
per-game ratio ranged 2.71x .. 21.07x; 95% CI on the mean [5.65, 13.03]
CORRECTION 2026-09-23: an earlier version of this note said a run at SOT_ALPHA0=0.7 gave
14.95x, and attributed the gap to the blend running both evaluators. That was wrong -- it
compared an n=2 run against this n=10 one, and the per-game ratio spans 2.71x..21.07x, so
the difference was sampling noise. A paired measurement over 6 seeds puts the blend's
throughput cost at ~1.6%. alpha0=0 is still pinned here, for the plain reason: this
experiment is about the NETWORK as an evaluator, so calibrate on the agent you will run.
The CI is wide enough that r should be re-derived from >=20 cluster games.
COST, read before submitting: r ~ 8 means ~78s of thinking per turn, an engine --timeout
near 90, roughly 18 minutes per game and about 120 core-hours for the 400 games. Submit
with an explicit --time=00:45:00; slurm_experiment.sh's 00:30:00 default would kill every
task. See experiments/configs/equal_effort_baseline_slowed.json for the same question asked
from the other direction at a normal row's cost -- run that one first, and read the two
together. This calibration serves both configs.
_how_to_fill_this_in: Runs the calibration block below (20 games, DeepSetsBotExp vs SakkirinaScaled, both at
stock speed) and prints mean evaluations per turn for each agent plus a SUGGESTED
2. Put that number into matchups[0].env.SOT_TIME_SCALE below, and set matchups[0].timeout to
ceil(9.8 * that scale) + 2 -- the engine clock has to be able to accommodate the bot's own
enlarged per-turn cap, or every turn ends as a TURN_TIMEOUT.
3. Re-run --calibrate with those values to CONFIRM the two evals/turn figures actually meet.
Evaluations per turn is only approximately linear in the time budget (tree reuse and the
rule-based fast paths do not scale with the clock), so the first suggestion is a starting
point, not an answer. Iterate until the two agents are within a few percent.
The harness REFUSES to run any matchup whose timeout or env still says TBD -- a run that
quietly fell back to SOT_TIME_SCALE=1.0 would produce a full set of numbers labelled
'equal effort' that measured nothing of the kind.

matchups.label: equal_effort
matchups.note: The baseline stays at 1.0 (stock SakkirinaSolo timing) on purpose -- it is the fixed point the treatment is matched TO. Only DeepSetsBotExp's clock moves. SOT_ALPHA0=0 makes this the pure-network agent (behaviourally DeepSetsBot); see _why_alpha0_is_zero above.

matchups.label: calibrate_stock_speed
matchups.note: SakkirinaScaled rather than SakkirinaSolo because stock SakkirinaSolo emits no throughput telemetry at all, and at SOT_BASELINE_TIME_SCALE=1.0 the two are timing-identical. This is how the stock baseline's evaluations per turn gets measured. SOT_ALPHA0=0 must match the matchup it is calibrating FOR -- calibrating at 0.7 and running at 0.0 would match the wrong agent's throughput.
